candidates.locator: Caput I — De Deo Rerum Omnium Creatore
candidates.phrase: Hic solus verus Deus bonitate sua et omnipotenti virtute
candidates.rationale: The official Latin conciliar text of Dei Filius predicates 'bonitate sua' (his own goodness) directly of the one true God, fully asserting the floor.
candidates.chunk_text: Sancta Catholica Apostolica Romana Ecclesia credit et confitetur, unum esse Deum verum et vivum, Creatorem ac Dominum caeli et terrae, omnipotentem, aeternum, immensum, in comprehensibilem, intellectu ac voluntate omnique perfectione infinitum: qui cum sit una singularis, simplex omnino et incommutabilis substantia spiritualis, praedicandus est re et essentia a mundo distinctus, in se et ex se beatissimus, et super omnia quae praeter ipsum sunt et concipi possunt, ineffabiliter excelsus. Hic solus verus Deus bonitate sua et omnipotenti virtute non ad augendam suam beatitudinem, nec ad acquirendam, sed ad manifestandam perfectionem suam per bona, quae creaturis impertitur, liberrimo consilio simul ab initio temporis utramque de nihilo condidit creaturam, spiritualem et corporalem, angelicam videlicet et mundanam, ac deinde humanam quasi communem ex spiritu et corpore constitutam (Conc. Later. IV c. Firmiter). Universa vero, quae condidit, Deus providentia sua tuetur atque gubernat, attingens a fine usque ad finem fortiter, et dissponens omnia suaviter (Sap. VIII, 1). Omnia enim nuda et aperta sunt oculis eius (Cf. Hebr. IV, 13), ea etiam, quae libera creaturarum actione futura sunt.

candidates.phrase: This one true God, in his goodness and almighty power
candidates.rationale: The council's own English witness renders the same article, predicating goodness directly of the one true God as an attribute he possesses in himself.
candidates.chunk_text: This one true God, in his goodness and almighty power and by an absolutely free plan, at the beginning of time created from nothing both spiritual and material creation, that is to say angelic and earthly, and then created human beings composed as it were of both spirit and body in common.. He created not to obtain or increase his own happiness, but to show forth his perfection in the goods which He bestows upon His creatures.

candidates.phrase: God in his goodness and wisdom reveals himself
candidates.rationale: The Compendium states plainly that God reveals himself in his goodness, asserting goodness as a divine attribute of God himself, the sentence's subject.
candidates.chunk_text: 6. What does God reveal to man? God in his goodness and wisdom reveals himself. With deeds and words, he reveals himself and his plan of loving goodness which he decreed from all eternity in Christ. According to this plan, all people by the grace of the Holy Spirit are to share in the divine life as adopted “sons” in the only begotten Son of God.
